newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares close mixed, seen fluctuating.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares close mixed, seen fluctuating.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed mixed on Tuesday with investors concentrating on second-tier shares, traders said. There would be no clear trend on the market for the next few days, they said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares fell by 0.46 percent to 175.70 on $10.60 million in volume.
Andrei Kukk, chief trader at Rinaco-Plus brokerage, said the market would fluctuate until President Boris Yeltsin underwent his heart operation scheduled for mid-November.
"Before Yeltsin's operation every day will be the same: a fall in the morning or evening and then a bounce to the middle of the range," he said.

Mikhail Khaleyev, chief trader at IK Alfa-Capital said leading shares were still affected by the delay in the next tranche of Russia's International Monetary Fund loan and the acquisition by Surgut Holding of Surgutneftegaz's whole new share issue.
"The buyers are in in the second-tier shares, and there are practically no Western sellers," he said.
Khaleyev said investors were still watching leading shares unsure of what to do, while second-tier shares were less sensitive to such news.
Novosibirksenergo was one of the gainers of the day with prices rising to $2.10 from $1.90 at Monday's close.
The Novosibirsk regional administration has decided to retain a 30 percent stake in Novosibirskenergo, sought by UES, which already owns 25 percent of the company.
KamAZ rose to $1.192 from $1.170 after the price hit support, Khaleyev said.
The market ignored news that KamAZ was lifted from the list of companies which the government threatened with bankruptcy proceedings for tax arrears, he said.
TsUM rose to $0.368 from $0.300, Gazprom edged down to $0.42 from $0.43, Norilsk Nickel fell to $6.24 from $6.35, Rostelekom rose to $2.47 from $2.44 and Irkutskenergo was $0.102 after $0.100.
